title: La Silla and the Milky Way
caption: La Silla Observatory under the Milky Way, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: The bright band of the Milky Way stretches overhead in this view of La Silla, ESO's original observatory. Several of the many telescopes on the site are visible below, 2400 meters up in Chile's Atacama Desert.

The site enjoys around 300 clear nights per year and excellent viewing conditions, and the clear view of our galaxy here shows why. Over time it became the largest astronomical observatory of its kind.

Many of its telescopes were pioneers, paving the way for new kinds of astronomical technology that later shaped whole new generations of telescopes. The Very Large Telescope had a forerunner in the New Technology Telescope (NTT), while the Swedish-ESO Submillimeter Telescope (SEST) prepared the ground for APEX and ALMA, observatories that study the sky at millimeter and submillimeter wavelengths.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken with a camera at an ESO site, in visible light. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long camera exposure gathers far more light than the eye can, so the Milky Way and faint stars appear brighter and richer than they would to someone standing there.

explore: La Silla marked the 50th anniversary of its inauguration in 2019, the year this image was released. Its scientific output still ranks it among the most productive observatories in the world, half a century after it opened.
alt: Several telescope domes on a mountain at night under the bright band of the Milky Way.
